I have a 10 year old XFX Gold Certified 850 Watt PSU. I have run it on a test bench and in half a dozen gaming rigs.

Yesterday I was pulling data off of an old PATA IDE SSD and after disconnecting the drive and going into the bios to disable the IDE controller, the machine never posted again.

I tried a standby motherboard I have and it didn't work either.

Eventually j brought out a bench PSU and got the 2nd board up and running.

So now I am leaning toward the XFX PSU finally gave up the ghost.

The PATA drive needed a 3.5" to 2.5" adapter with a +5v pigtail. I've used them before, and the rail the pigtail was connected to on the PSU was already in use powering a 3.5" Sata drive.

Could this very minor additional load for a few hours have been enough to find a failure in the PSU?

Or is this yet another cosmic coincidence that cost me half a day of work?
PATA pulls more power than SATA so that could theoretically cause some issues. But I usually have seen that under the opposite usage, PATA powering SATA with an adapter can fry the SATA device.
The micro pc that the PATA SSD came from would also not post. However it did run long enough for me to dd the entire device with no errors.
You might want to open up the power supply to check for bad capacitors. If there is one, you can cheaply replace it.

Opening it up is dangerous, better to check the rails with a multimeter first and make sure 5v is 5v, etc.
